fields: Do Not Start With This When

rows.Main Input: single-cell or spatial expression grouped by cell identity, with ligand-receptor database context
rows.Main Use in This Topic: infer and visualize cell-group communication networks from ligand-receptor expression patterns
rows.Main Output: cell-group communication network and pathway-level interaction summaries
rows.Key Difference: Broad ecosystem baseline for network-level CCC interpretation; spatial proximity is not the core discriminator unless spatial context is added upstream.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 33597522; DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9; Layer 1 input code link
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the CellChat method-paper identity and public code link from the frozen input. The spatial-use caveat and comparator placement are Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: a widely adopted ligand-receptor communication network baseline is needed for annotated cell groups or clusters
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the primary question requires spatially variable LR statistics, relay-chain detection, causal intracellular pathways, or neighborhood-preference scoring as the main output
rows.Spatial Specificity: spatial use case; not intrinsically spatial-first
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: false-positive communication edges and loss of spatial context if proximity or tissue structure is not modeled explicitly

rows.Main Input: spatial expression with cell or spot coordinates, ligand-receptor pairs, and optional annotations
rows.Main Use in This Topic: detect single-cell or spot-level ligand-receptor and relay-network communication patterns
rows.Main Output: direct and relay CCC edges with attention/confidence-style scores and visualization-ready graph outputs
rows.Key Difference: Targets relay-network communication with a graph attention and contrastive-learning formulation rather than only pairwise LR co-expression.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 40481363; DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02721-3; PMC code-availability section
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method paper, DOI/PMID, open-source GitHub, and paper-local benchmarks. High scale sensitivity and branch placement are Layer 2 synthesized judgment from graph/deep-learning design and reported benchmark scope.
rows.Best First Choice When: single-cell or spot-level relay-network CCC is the main scientific question and graph-model complexity is acceptable
rows.Do Not Start With This When: a simple interpretable LR baseline, CPU-only conservative workflow, or purely group-level summary is preferred
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: LR database plus optional cell annotations
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: deep graph attention scores can be difficult to calibrate biologically, and paper-local benchmarks do not establish universal superiority

rows.Main Input: spatial expression, coordinates, and ligand-receptor/pathway priors
rows.Main Use in This Topic: screen spatial CCC by modeling communication as collective transport over tissue space
rows.Main Output: spatial communication directions, LR/pathway-level signals, and downstream communication summaries
rows.Key Difference: Uses collective optimal transport to represent sender-receiver communication over spatial geometry.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 36690742; DOI 10.1038/s41592-022-01728-4; Layer 1 input code link
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity and code link from the frozen input. The scale cue and closest-alternative comparison are Layer 2 synthesized judgment from optimal-transport problem structure.
rows.Best First Choice When: spatial sender-receiver geometry and directional communication flow are central to the analysis question
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the target is causal intracellular pathway reconstruction, broad non-spatial CCC baseline reporting, or neighborhood preference without expression/LR modeling
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: transport-based signals depend on spatial scale, LR priors, and expression preprocessing; inferred direction is not causal proof

rows.Main Input: sender/receiver expression, candidate ligands, target gene signatures, and prior ligand-target network
rows.Main Use in This Topic: link candidate ligands to receiver target-gene programs for communication interpretation
rows.Main Output: ranked ligands and ligand-target regulatory links
rows.Key Difference: Prioritizes ligands by downstream target-gene regulatory potential rather than only LR co-expression.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 31819264; DOI 10.1038/s41592-019-0667-5; Layer 1 input code link
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity and public code link from the frozen input. Its use for spatial CCC is Layer 2 synthesized judgment because the original method is not spatial-first.
rows.Best First Choice When: the task is to connect sender ligands to receiver transcriptional programs or pathway interpretation
rows.Do Not Start With This When: spatial proximity, spatially variable LR interfaces, or neighborhood-preference statistics are the central selection criteria
rows.Spatial Specificity: non-spatial baseline with spatial use case
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: prior-network bias and indirect regulatory links can be overinterpreted as direct spatial communication

rows.Main Input: single-cell expression, spatial locations or mapped cell positions, and signaling gene sets
rows.Main Use in This Topic: infer spatial and signaling relationships between cells using optimal transport
rows.Main Output: spatial mapping and inferred signaling relationships
rows.Key Difference: Early optimal-transport route that links spatial mapping and signaling inference, preceding more CCC-specialized transport workflows.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 32350282; DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5; Layer 1 input code link
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity and code link from the frozen input. Its role as an early/boundary spatial signaling method is Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: the analysis needs an early transport-based spatial/signaling relationship model or compatibility with prior SpaOTsc workflows
rows.Do Not Start With This When: a newer dedicated spatial CCC method, relay-network model, or spatially variable LR statistic is clearly required
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: expression and spatial mapping inputs; annotations may be useful
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: boundary between spatial mapping and communication inference can blur method interpretation

rows.Main Input: spatial expression, cell-type or spot annotations, LR pairs, and knowledge-graph context
rows.Main Use in This Topic: infer spatially resolved CCC with knowledge-graph-supported LR relationships
rows.Main Output: LR-mediated communication events and pathway-style interaction summaries
rows.Key Difference: Uses knowledge-graph structure to connect LR interactions with spatially resolved transcriptomic data.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 35908020; DOI 10.1038/s41467-022-32111-8; Layer 1 input code link
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity and code link from the frozen input. Comparator and scale cautions are Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: knowledge-graph-supported spatial LR inference is preferred over a simpler LR co-expression baseline
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the task is specifically neighborhood preference without expression, relay networks, or causal intracellular pathway tracing
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: cell annotations plus LR/knowledge graph resources
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: knowledge-base coverage and annotation quality may dominate inferred communication structure

rows.Main Input: spatial expression, coordinates, and LR database
rows.Main Use in This Topic: identify spatially co-expressed LR pairs and associated CCC patterns
rows.Main Output: significant spatial LR pairs and communication-pattern summaries
rows.Key Difference: Focuses on statistical detection of spatially co-expressed LR pairs rather than transport flow or broad network visualization.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 37414760; DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-39608-w; Layer 1 input code link
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity and code link from the frozen input. The scale and branch-local comparator cues are Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: the question is whether LR pairs are spatially co-expressed or patterned across tissue space
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the desired output is relay-chain communication, causal intracellular paths, or neighborhood preference over cell labels alone
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: LR database; annotations may be useful
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: co-expression can reflect colocalization, abundance, or preprocessing effects rather than direct communication

rows.Main Input: paired or aligned spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq expression with spatial affinities
rows.Main Use in This Topic: single-cell-resolution CCC prediction using graph attention and subgraph modeling
rows.Main Output: predicted single-cell CCC patterns and graph-attention outputs
rows.Key Difference: Uses subgraph-based graph attention and scRNA/ST integration for single-cell-resolution spatial CCC.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 39155292; DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-51329-2; PMC code-availability section
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the paper title, DOI/PMID, and DeepTalk code link. Human review approved `DeepTalk` as the unified method identity because the verified publication/code identity is DeepTalk. Resource and scale cues are Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: single-cell-resolution spatial CCC is needed and paired scRNA/ST integration is part of the intended analysis
rows.Do Not Start With This When: no suitable scRNA reference or pairing exists, or a simpler cell-group LR summary is sufficient
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: scRNA reference / aligned paired data plus LR context
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: reference mismatch and graph-model complexity can create confident-looking but hard-to-validate CCC calls

rows.Main Input: spatial expression, coordinates, optional image-derived tissue structure, and LR pairs
rows.Main Use in This Topic: support LR interaction analysis within a broader spatial trajectory and tissue-context workflow
rows.Main Output: LR interaction scores and related spatial/trajectory outputs
rows.Key Difference: CCC support is embedded in a broader spatiotemporal/trajectory mapping framework rather than being only a CCC method.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 38007580; DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-43120-6; Layer 1 input code link
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity and code link from the frozen input. The method-family leakage caveat is Layer 2 synthesized judgment and is inherited from the input notes.
rows.Best First Choice When: CCC interpretation is needed alongside stLearn trajectory or tissue-context analyses already in scope
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the task is a dedicated CCC benchmark, relay-network inference, or spatially variable LR test without trajectory context
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: method-family leakage: CCC findings can be entangled with broader trajectory or tissue-structure modeling

rows.Main Input: cell coordinates, cell-type labels, and sample/cohort grouping for neighborhood preference analysis
rows.Main Use in This Topic: quantify cellular neighbor preferences and compare tissue-neighborhood signatures
rows.Main Output: neighbor-preference scores for cell-type pairs and cohort-level comparison features
rows.Key Difference: Focuses on conditional neighbor-preference scoring over cell labels, not LR expression or pathway inference.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 41986357; DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-71699-z; PMC code-availability section
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the benchmark paper, COZI implementations, and comparison framework. Its placement as a CCC neighborhood branch rather than LR inference is Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: the biological question is cell-type neighbor preference or cohort-level tissue-architecture differences rather than LR expression
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the desired output is ligand-receptor pairs, sender-receiver expression flow, relay networks, or intracellular pathway causality
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: neighbor preference can reflect segmentation, annotation, sampling density, and cohort structure rather than molecular communication

rows.Main Input: spatially resolved marker or expression features with configurable spatial views and targets
rows.Main Use in This Topic: model how local or broader spatial contexts explain target cell or marker behavior
rows.Main Output: view-specific importance and variance-explained style interaction summaries
rows.Key Difference: Uses multiview predictive modeling to quantify contextual influence rather than direct LR-pair communication.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 35422018; DOI 10.1186/s13059-022-02663-5; Layer 1 input code link; COZI/NEP benchmark PMID 41986357 for branch-local comparison context
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the MISTy method-paper identity and code link. Its NEP-branch use and comparison against COZI-style neighbor methods are supported by benchmark context but remain branch-local, not global ranking evidence.
rows.Best First Choice When: the question is how multiple spatial context views predict markers, cell types, or interaction effects
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the question requires explicit LR-pair calls or a simple interpretable neighbor-preference score
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: features and target definitions; annotations often useful
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: predictive importance can be mistaken for mechanism, and view definitions can drive conclusions

rows.Main Input: spatial expression with cellular neighborhoods or bags and interaction labels/features
rows.Main Use in This Topic: map cellular interactions from spatially resolved transcriptomics with probabilistic interaction modeling
rows.Main Output: predicted cellular interaction signals and spatial interaction maps
rows.Key Difference: Uses Bayesian multiple-instance-style modeling for spatial interaction inference rather than LR co-expression alone.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity. Code access was not confirmed in the bounded PubMed/PMC pass, so access and implementation cues remain unclear. Comparator placement is Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: probabilistic spatial interaction modeling is the key method family to evaluate for a dataset
rows.Do Not Start With This When: confirmed public code access is required before method selection, or the desired output is explicit LR-pair ranking
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: unclear; likely depends on interaction labels or features
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: implementation availability and external benchmark coverage remain weaker than for older open packages

rows.Main Input: spatial molecular data with cell or spatial neighborhoods and feature measurements
rows.Main Use in This Topic: partition spatial molecular variance into cell-cell interaction or neighborhood components
rows.Key Difference: Frames interaction as variance decomposition rather than LR-pair inference or predictive multiview modeling.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 31577949; DOI 10.1016/j.celrep.2019.08.077; Layer 1 input code link
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity and code link from the frozen input. Its placement in the interaction-effect branch is Layer 2 synthesized judgment from method family and current Layer 1 scope.
rows.Best First Choice When: variance partitioning of spatial molecular interaction effects is the intended statistical framing
rows.Do Not Start With This When: explicit LR pairs, relay graphs, or causal pathway reconstruction are the desired outputs
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: spatial molecular features and model design
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: variance components depend strongly on model assumptions and can be hard to translate into direct biological communication claims

rows.Main Input: spatial expression, LR pairs, downstream genes/transcription factors, and spatial interface profiles
rows.Main Use in This Topic: identify spatially variable ligand-receptor interactions with downstream functional support
rows.Main Output: spatially variable LR interactions and functionally supported interface-level signals
rows.Key Difference: Adds downstream functional support to spatially variable LR interaction detection rather than testing LR co-expression alone.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 40841363; DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-62988-0; PMC code-availability section
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the method-paper identity, code link, tutorials, and comparison against several spatial/statistical tools. The branch-local role is Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: the task asks for spatially variable LR interactions and downstream-gene functional support
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the intended analysis is broad cell-group CCC networks, neighbor preference without expression, or causal intracellular pathway tracing
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: LR database and downstream gene/TF support resources
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: downstream support can strengthen plausibility but does not remove database bias or prove causality

rows.Main Input: single-cell expression with cell-level CCC features; spatial use cases may add tissue context
rows.Main Use in This Topic: compare cell-cell communication at single-cell resolution, especially across cells or conditions
rows.Main Output: single-cell-level CCC comparison features and interaction summaries
rows.Key Difference: Focuses on comparative single-cell CCC rather than a spatial-first LR or neighborhood model.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the paper identity and single-cell CCC comparison framing. Bounded PMC code-link retrieval was blocked by a browser challenge, so code access is not asserted. Spatial relevance is Layer 2 synthesized judgment from the frozen input and paper scope.
rows.Best First Choice When: the analysis emphasizes single-cell-level comparative CCC rather than spatial-first interface or neighbor modeling
rows.Do Not Start With This When: confirmed code access is required immediately or spatial proximity is the core signal to model
rows.Spatial Specificity: single-cell CCC with spatial use cases
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: single-cell CCC comparison may not itself validate spatial contact or molecular mechanism

rows.Main Input: single-cell or spatial expression plus LR pairs from existing CCC methods or user-defined inputs
rows.Main Use in This Topic: explore intracellular causal pathways linking CCC inputs across interacting cell types
rows.Main Output: interactive causal pathway reconstructions and communication-pathway visualizations
rows.Key Difference: Acts as a pathway-aware causal interpretation layer over CCC inputs rather than a primary LR discovery method.
rows.Evidence Source: PubMed PMID 40366019; DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaf404; PMC availability statement
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence verifies the web-server method paper and public web-server URL. Source-code availability is not asserted. Causal-overinterpretation caveat is Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: LR calls already exist and the next question is intracellular pathway interpretation across interacting cell types
rows.Do Not Start With This When: the task is primary discovery of spatial LR pairs, neighbor preference, or execution through local package code
rows.Spatial Specificity: accepts spatial or single-cell CCC inputs
rows.Reference / Annotation Dependence: input LR pairs and expression-defined cell groups
rows.Primary Scientific Risk: causal language depends on model assumptions and input CCC calls; output should not be treated as experimental causality
